moments.action: A long held take: the young driver in the black tee stands alone at the roadside, back to camera, looking down the mountain road as it falls away in a chain of blue marker lights. He never moves off.

Cut wide to the gathering point above a floodlit dam, cars and people lining the ledge, then in among them: the kid in the red-and-white striped track jacket works a phone as spectators crowd the lot.

Heads in the crowd all turn one way. The heavyset bald man breaks off, strides over and hauls open the door of a black sedan; a hard-faced man in a dark coat is already standing over it as a woman gets out.

Reverse on the onlookers staring back, the foreign kids blurred behind them, then the reason walks in: an older man in a black fedora and overcoat, flanked by two minders, passing the woman in fur who turns to watch.

In the crowd a dark-haired boy flips open his phone and reads the screen while the girl beside him keeps her eyes on the arrivals; the next shot drops almost to black on the kid in the striped jacket beside a car.

Hard cut away from the crowd to the pass itself: a rush of blurred night road, black trees and verge tearing past the lens, the camera flying downhill until figures and pale rock smear by at the roadside.
The ride settles into one long run down the empty two-lane, bending through the dark hillside; a painted arrow flicks under the camera and a lit truck sits parked on the shoulder further down.

Inside his car the young American shuts his eyes a beat with lights ahead; then from above three cars are already running the mountain road, tail-lights flaring, and the rival driver sits locked over his wheel.
